reason: This passage from 1 Samuel 9-10 depicts Hebrew leaders (Samuel and the newly anointed Saul) as beneficent toward the Hebrew people. Samuel anoints Saul specifically to 'save' the people from Philistine oppression (וְהוֹשִׁ֥יעַ אֶת־ עַמִּ֖י מִיַּ֣ד פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים). When Saul is presented to the people, they respond enthusiastically with 'Long live the king!' (יְחִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ), demonstrating popular support. The only antagonistic elements mentioned are 'sons of Belial' (בְנֵי בְלִיַּעַל) who despise Saul, but these are presented as marginal dissenters, not as leaders. Samuel's entire role is to serve as an intermediary between God and the people, mediating their salvation.
